cells.tense: You're choosing it right now, with your hands in it, and you know it's a choice.
cells.verb: joining your stream to another's and tending what the two of you make
cells.place: in the care you're already giving what's growing
cells.ask: offer one more stretch of tending than feels safe, and let what you've built together carry you forward — direction comes from genuine engagement, not from pushing the pace.
cells.core:
Two streams are meeting in you and one flow is coming out. You're not deliberating about it anymore — you've decided, and the deciding shows in how you tend what's growing between you. The connection isn't a hope or a maybe; it's a fact you're living in, and you're feeding it deliberately.

The care you give has a direction now. It isn't care in general, spilled everywhere — it's care for this, and the choosing is what makes it land.
cells.sheetLine: You've chosen this connection, and you're feeding it on purpose.

cells.tense: Ahead of you there's a version where the connection is already proven, and you're living there.
cells.verb: forcing the merge before it's ready, gripping what hasn't finished forming
cells.place: in the growing thing you won't let grow at its own speed
cells.ask: let one thing take its own time for a day — growth happens without forcing, with care that doesn't exhaust and space held without clutching.
cells.core:
You're holding the growing thing so tightly it can't move. Before it's asked for, before it's yours to decide, you've already arranged how it will go — and the tending has turned into steering. You're exhausted and the thing is stunted, and you're still bracing ahead toward a version of this that hasn't arrived.

The grip feels like devotion. From inside the grip it's hard to tell the difference. But what you're protecting the connection from is the connection.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding the growing thing so tightly it can't grow.

cells.tense: There's a door behind you that you're still standing at.
cells.verb: withholding the merge, tending from a distance where nothing can reach you
cells.place: in the care you give without ever arriving in it
cells.ask: put one honest perception in front of someone this week — direct knowing lands without argument, and comfort with not-knowing is part of it.
cells.core:
You're caring for something that's growing and you're not in the room while you do it. Somewhere back there the merge didn't hold, or you never said yes to it, and you've been tending from behind glass ever since — present in the tasks, absent in the meeting.

What's missing isn't devotion. It's the arrival. You can't merge with what you won't come close to, and you can't tend what you won't touch.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending something you won't come close to.

cells.tense: Your pen is down, and you're still writing — you just haven't picked it up in your own name.
cells.verb: merging by instinct and calling it just how things happened
cells.place: in the care you give as if it were simply your nature
cells.ask: say out loud that you chose one thing you're tending — practice flows without force when it isn't run on proving something.
cells.core:
You've already joined your current to something else and you're already tending what comes of it. The choosing happened; the saying-so didn't. You describe it as just what you do, or how the situation is, or nothing in particular — while the direction you've given your care is doing real work every day.

What you're calling circumstances is your own hand. The stream is flowing in a direction, and you're the one who pointed it there.
cells.sheetLine: You've already chosen this. You're calling it just how things are.
